subject: Communication
title: Eye Contact: The Social Glue
description: A short lesson to help you apply Eye Contact: The Social Glue.

hook.text: Hold eye contact for 3 seconds: connection. Hold it for 10 seconds: intimidation. Timing is everything.

buildup.text: Eye contact activates the social brain network, triggering trust, attention, and emotional processing.

discovery.text: Comfortable eye contact lasts 3-5 seconds. Breaking first signals submission; holding too long signals dominance.

twist.text: In some cultures, direct eye contact with elders is disrespectful. The 'right amount' is culturally coded.

climax.text: Liars don't always avoid eye contact — some overcompensate. It's the change from baseline that matters.

punchline.text: Eyes are windows. How long you look through them is the message.

quiz.question: What does comfortable eye contact typically last?

details.summary: Eye contact regulates conversation flow, signals attention, and builds trust. Too little suggests disinterest or deception; too much can feel aggressive. The optimal amount varies by culture and context.
details.whyItMatters: Mastering eye contact norms enhances rapport and persuasion while avoiding the discomfort of getting it wrong.
takeaways: Eye contact signals attention, trust, and engagement
Optimal duration varies by culture and social setting
Breaking eye contact downward signals submission or thought

faq.question: Why does prolonged eye contact feel uncomfortable?
faq.answer: Extended gaze activates the autonomic nervous system and can be perceived as a dominance signal or threat. The discomfort likely evolved as a protective mechanism against potential aggression from strangers.

faq.question: How does eye contact differ across cultures?
faq.answer: In Western cultures, direct eye contact signals honesty and confidence. In many East Asian and Indigenous cultures, avoiding direct gaze shows respect, especially toward elders or authority figures.
